A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCALINGVIS/ADAPTVIS study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original attention analyses, spatial-reasoning experiments, benchmark comparisons, and supplementary robustness results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical results and adds Qwen2-VL benchmark evaluations and attention/confidence analyses in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The attention scaling and confidence-dependent intervention procedures in Equations 2–3 remain unchanged. Applying the existing intervention to Qwen2-VL introduces no documented algorithmic component or adaptation.

E1.justification: v3 adds TextVQA evaluation in Appendix B, extending coverage to text-reading visual question answering. WhatsUp, VSR, POPE, GQA, and VQAv2 are retained; testing Qwen2-VL on existing datasets does not itself expand task coverage.

E2.justification: New Appendix B comparisons include unmodified Qwen2-VL as the reference against attention intervention. The existing LLaVA, VCD, and DoLa comparisons remain unchanged, with no additional decoding baseline.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluations using Qwen2-VL and an attention analysis reporting average scores per text/image token. Existing LLaVA splits, prompts, metrics, and tuning ranges are retained. The changed overlap plots lack an explanation establishing whether their calculation protocol changed.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds tests of whether image-attention sparsity and the confidence–accuracy relationship extend to Qwen2-VL. Figures 21–24 revise the existing real-image overlap analysis, while the earlier prompt, reversal, hyperparameter-transfer, and error analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new Qwen2-VL 'Unc.' entries continue the existing model-confidence diagnostics rather than introducing statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 3–6 add substantial Qwen2-VL results, including VG two-object scores of 56.22 without intervention and 66.95 with intervention. Figures 21–24 replace overlap distributions and AUROCs; for example, Figure 21's layer-1 AUROC changes from 0.505 to 0.573. Their unexplained scale changes preclude treating these as comparable performance gains. Original Tables 1–2 are identical.

T1.justification: The attention equations and entropy/skewness definitions remain unchanged. No new formal assumptions, mathematical derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about attention location, confidence-guided intervention, and improvements up to 50 absolute points. The Qwen2-VL experiments add support without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B adds the explanation that general QA benefits less because object-presence questions depend less on spatial attention geometry. It also interprets Qwen2-VL findings as support for cross-model generality. Appendix A's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The disclosed hyperparameter grids, 20% validation sampling, command-line instructions, timing information, and code/data links are retained. The Qwen2-VL addition supplies no specific checkpoint-size, tuning, or hardware details.

R1.justification: v3 adds Singh et al. (2019), the TextVQA reference. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to attention calibration, PASTA, and hallucination-reduction methods otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited grammatical and heading edits, adds acknowledgments and publication information, and moves Broad Impact from Appendix B into the main Impact Statement. The new Qwen2-VL section occupies Appendix B; the overall narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds four Qwen2-VL tables, redraws Figures 21–24 with changed histograms and axes, adjusts Figure 6's styling and ticks, and relocates Figure 8. Most existing displays retain their structure and the overall layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: The Qwen2-VL evaluations and diagnostic analyses provide useful evidence beyond the LLaVA family, while TextVQA modestly broadens validation. These gains are limited by sparse Qwen-specific reproducibility details, inconsistent method/table references in Appendix B, and unexplained changes to the overlap plots. The core method and main results remain unchanged.
